classification.difficultyReason: Interpret equal vectors and perpendicularity, then apply a quadrilateral test with reasons.

content.prompt:
In the diagram, $\overrightarrow{BA}=\overrightarrow{CD}$ and $\overrightarrow{BA}\perp\overrightarrow{AD}$.

What type of special quadrilateral is ABCD? Give reasons for your answer.

spec.description: Unshaded quadrilateral with A upper left, B lower left, C lower right and D upper right; arrows B to A, C to D and A to D. Ordinary source strokes use house black.
spec.mathematics: One pair of opposite sides is equal and parallel; adjacent sides BA and AD are perpendicular.
spec.answerVisibility: All vertices and directional arrows are permanent student givens.

answer.short: Rectangle. Opposite sides BA and CD are equal and parallel, and $\angle BAD=90^\circ$.
answer.worked: Since $\overrightarrow{BA}=\overrightarrow{CD}$, opposite sides BA and CD are parallel and equal. Hence ABCD is a parallelogram. Also, $\overrightarrow{BA}\perp\overrightarrow{AD}$ gives $\angle BAD=90^\circ$. A parallelogram with a right angle is a rectangle.
